name: Varunprasaath R. Selvaraju, Ph.D.
summary: PhD chemist/materials scientist with 6+ years in thin-film and optical materials characterization, spectroscopic/ellipsometric workflows, DOE/SPC, and technical documentation. Builds reproducible measurement models and process-property datasets that translate spectroscopy, film quality, and troubleshooting data into engineering decisions.

education.details:
Dissertation: Modular Design and Electrochemical Properties of Xanthene-Based Electrochromic Materials
Advisor: Prof. Seth Marder
(Transferred from Georgia Institute of Technology)

education.degree: B.S. (Research), Major: Chemistry; Minor: Materials Science
education.details: INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (Top 1% nationally)

bullets: Lead DOE-guided process-development studies for bio-based polymer systems, defining analytical readouts, process windows, reproducibility criteria, and SOP-ready specifications.
Translate FT-IR, thermal-analysis, spectroscopy, and process data into technical recommendations that support measurement repeatability and material-quality decisions.

Designed and characterized 15+ electrochromic material variants using UV-Vis-NIR, FT-IR, spectroelectrochemistry, cyclic voltammetry, ellipsometry-informed optical analysis, NMR, GPC, TGA, DSC, and MS-informed interpretation.
Built structure-property-processing datasets connecting optical response, stability, purity, and degradation signals to material design and troubleshooting recommendations.
Co-led AFOSR-funded thin-film coating process development, linking CVD/surface-preparation conditions to morphology, interface quality, optical performance, and reproducible process controls.
Optimized polymer thin-film deposition with DOE strategies and in-situ QCM-D process monitoring to quantify growth kinetics, coating uniformity, and process repeatability.
Managed operations for a 15-member process-development laboratory, implementing equipment tracking, calibration routines, SOPs, and safety protocols that improved instrument uptime by 30%.
Trained researchers on instrument workflows, experimental documentation, and safe handling while coordinating multiple concurrent materials-development projects.
